title: Charity football match to honour boxing legend Ricky Hatton

evidence_packet.title: Charity football match to honour boxing legend Ricky Hatton
evidence_packet.lead: The fundraiser is being held at Manchester City's Joie Stadium in memory of the Hyde boxer
evidence_packet.summary: The fundraiser is being held at Manchester City's Joie Stadium in memory of the Hyde boxer
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Charity football match to honour boxing legend Ricky Hatton - BBC News Image source, Press Association Image caption, Ricky 'The Hitman' Hatton, a world champion at light-welterweight and welterweight, was one of Britain's most popular fighters Published 1 hour ago A charity football match in memory of boxing legend Ricky Hatton will take place later. Game 4 Ricky, at City Football Academy's Joie Stadium, will feature celebrities, ex-professional footballers and boxers playing in teams captained by Hatton's son Campbell and brother Matthew. Hyde boxer Ricky Hatton - known as "The Hitman" - won world titles at light-welterweight and welterweight and was one of Britain's most popular fighters. He died last year aged 46. Hatton's beloved Manchester City said money raised from the game would support mental health initiatives under its City in the Community programme. Hatton won 45 of his 48 professional bouts during a glittering 15-year career. The charity football match kicks off at 14:15 GMT with Team Hitman taking on Team Hatton. Singer Russell Watson will also be making a special half-time performance at the stadium. 'Inspiration' Team Hitman's line up includes rapper Big Zuu, singer-songwriter, footballer and presenter Chelcee Grimes, and former England goalkeeper David James, as well as former world boxing champion Johnny Nelson. Meanwhile, Team Hatton features former City goalkeeper Joe Hart, comedian Jason Manford and WBC light-welterweight world champion Dalton Smith plus YouTuber and presenter Harry Pinero. Former footballer Ben Mee, who grew up in Sale and came through Man City's academy, is also in Team Hatton. Mee, who met Hatton a few times, said he was honoured to be playing in the event. "He was always a kind character for fans," he told BBC Radio Manchester

title: The day celebrated cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin paid Manchester a visit

evidence_packet.title: The day celebrated cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin paid Manchester a visit
evidence_packet.lead: Sixty-five years ago Yuri Gagarin became the first person to journey into space
evidence_packet.summary: Sixty-five years ago Yuri Gagarin became the first person to journey into space
evidence_packet.evidence_text: You could easily miss it, but a small black plaque sits in a corner of the arrivals hall at Manchester Airport's Terminal 3 to commemorate one of humanity's greatest achievements It marks the incredible journey of Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin, who famously became the first person in space 65 years ago On 12 April 1961, his Vostok spacecraft completed a single orbit of the Earth at the height of the so-called space race, as Russia and the US competed to make the first daring leaps beyond the heavens Just three months later, Gagarin visited Manchester to be greeted by rapturous crowds as part of a world tour on 12 July 1961. His visit is the subject of a new episode of Hidden Manchester on BBC Sounds Hundreds of people turned out to see Gagarin arrive at the airport, including Fred Garner who spoke to the BBC in 2011 "You could tell he was in uniform with like a rubber cape on. I can't believe how hard it was raining," he said

title: How Hollyoaks storyline hopes to shine a light on grooming

evidence_packet.title: How Hollyoaks storyline hopes to shine a light on grooming
evidence_packet.lead: Actress Brooke Vincent wants to raise awareness of the importance of understanding abuse of power
evidence_packet.summary: Actress Brooke Vincent wants to raise awareness of the importance of understanding abuse of power
evidence_packet.evidence_text: How Hollyoaks storyline hopes to shine a light on grooming - BBC News Image source, Channel 4/Lime Pictures Image caption, Actress Brooke Vincent plays teacher Abigail Matthews in the Channel 4 soap By Lauren Hirst North West Published 1 hour ago When soap star Brooke Vincent first heard of the upcoming grooming storyline in Hollyoaks, she knew it was important story she wanted to help tell. After leaving the role of Sophie Webster on Coronation Street after 17 years, it promised the opportunity to play a completely different role as teacher Abigail Matthews. "When I did my audition, it was very much set in stone the kind of story it was going to be," said Vincent who grew up in Tameside, Greater Manchester. "To be honest, it was that that made me really want it. "Obviously, when you do auditions, you want the job, but I think with this one, it was just something that I just felt was such an important story to be told." In a long-running storyline, teenager Dee-Dee Hutchinson, played by Chloe Atkinson, has grown close to the Hollyoaks High teacher played by Vincent. Dee-Dee is unaware of the legal boundaries between adults in positions of authority and young people. And, in a dark twist, they are currently preparing to start a new life together abroad. Image source, Channel 4/Lime Pictures Image caption, Abigail asks Dee Dee to run away together to start a new life in France "Not every person who has bad intentions looks a certain way or acts a certain way," Vincent continued. "It can very much be hidden in plain sight, which is exactly where Abigail is. "So it is just keeping the younger generation aware of things that aren't appropriate, what you should be looking out for and what you can do to seek help if you do find yourself in that horrible situation." evidence_packet.summary: Police say a 27-year-old man died after being stabbed in the "shocking and tragic attack" in Crumpsall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A murder investigation has been launched after a 27-year-old man was stabbed in Manchester Officers were called to Moss Bank in the Crumpsall area of the city shortly after 01:30 GMT following reports that a man had suffered several stab wounds. He later died from his injuries in an ambulance Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said initial inquiries suggested the victim had been attacked by "a number of males" all believed to have been wearing dark clothing and balaclavas The suspects are believed to have fled the scene in the direction of Ash Tree Road, said a force spokesperson who added that no arrests had been made and inquiries were continuing Forensics officers could be seen lifting drain covers within the area and looking under cars parked along the street lined with terraced houses A police spokesperson said the victim's family had been informed and were being supported by specially trained officers

title: Residents feel 'let down' in troubled Greater Manchester road

evidence_packet.title: Residents feel 'let down' in troubled Greater Manchester road
evidence_packet.lead: Baguley Crescent residents complain about fly-tipping, a condemned building and anti-social behaviour
evidence_packet.summary: Baguley Crescent residents complain about fly-tipping, a condemned building and anti-social behaviour
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents feel 'let down' in troubled Greater Manchester road - BBC News Image caption, Patrick Connelly says he feels he has been constantly "let down" by his landlord By Richard Stead North West Published 14 November 2026 Baguley Crescent has long been blighted by fly-tipping, a condemned building and anti-social behaviour. I have been reporting on life on this small Greater Manchester estate - located just off the M60 between Prestwich and Middleton - for years. But what I saw when speaking to some social housing tenants about a recent fire - in which a man in his 60s died - really shocked me. Residents here feel forgotten by the very authorities that are supposed to look out for them. Local MPs have claimed that police officers - fearing for their own safety - have been too afraid to patrol the road. And, despite years of complaints, they say the area has seen little improvement. Image source, BBC/Richard Stead Image caption, The area has been blighted by persistent fly-tipping despite council clear-up efforts Patrick Connelly, an 80-year-old who lives in the apartment block where the fire took place, showed me round his flat. "Almost 10 years ago I told my social landlord that my cooker didn't work and there was no response, so my daughter bought me an air-fryer... but it means I can't have my grandchildren round for a Sunday lunch." Patrick, who has lived on Baguley Crescent for 17 years, added: "I've asked to move several times because of the anti-social behaviour on this road but the housing association keeps letting me down - all they've done is paint the walls a few years ago." title: What do Christmas market traders say about rising prices?

evidence_packet.title: What do Christmas market traders say about rising prices?
evidence_packet.lead: From £8 bratwursts to £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps, why is the cost of the markets rising year on year?
evidence_packet.summary: From £8 bratwursts to £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps, why is the cost of the markets rising year on year?
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mention Christmas markets these days and the conversation often turns to rising prices – from £8 bratwursts, £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps and even £5 for a few marshmallow sticks But what do the people behind the stalls think? Are they benefiting from the hikes or are their own profits being squeezed? Traders at Manchester's Christmas markets told the BBC they were feeling the pressure of increasing bills for staff, ingredients and energy, with some saying they were making less money despite charging more One trader said it costs at least £4,000 a day to run each her four stalls, while another has cut prices to keep customers coming back Nils Borstel, 25, helps run Bratwurst King, a family business which has operated at the markets since 1999 He said a sausage that previously cost £3.50 now sold for £8, with much of the increase taking place over the past five or six years

title: Peter Hook: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 'is for fans and Ian Curtis'

evidence_packet.title: Peter Hook: Rock & Roll Hall of Fame 'is for fans and Ian Curtis'
evidence_packet.lead: Joy Division and New Order will be jointly inducted to the Hall of Fame later, along with Oasis
evidence_packet.summary: Joy Division and New Order will be jointly inducted to the Hall of Fame later, along with Oasis
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Peter Hook said he would be thrilled to pick up the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame award later on behalf of Joy Division and New Order "for Ian Curtis and for all our fans" The Salford musician will be in Los Angeles to receive the accolade. Fellow Manchester band Oasis will also be inducted but are not expected to attend the ceremony Joy Division and New Order have been given the award jointly - with the late Ian Curtis, Bernard Sumner, Stephen Morris and Gillian Gilbert being honoured alongside Hook Bassist Hook said he was going to the ceremony as a "thank you" to the fans as "without them we'd be absolutely nothing" Hook, a founding member of Joy Division, wrote on Instagram he was "wonderfully pleased" with the honour and that he had been "looking forward to it for years" He ended by saying "I will see you on the night," presenting a conundrum for his former bandmates, with whom he is not on speaking terms following a protracted legal battle

title: Woman with bowel condition turned away from disabled toilets

evidence_packet.title: Woman with bowel condition turned away from disabled toilets
evidence_packet.lead: A woman with Crohn's disease says she has been denied access to facilities due to a lack of understanding
evidence_packet.summary: A woman with Crohn's disease says she has been denied access to facilities due to a lack of understanding
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A woman with Crohn's disease has told how she has been denied access to accessible toilets by people who do not understand the condition, and has even been asked to "prove" she has a disability Victoria Danson was diagnosed with the chronic inflammatory bowel condition when she was 19, and is also undergoing treatment for a form of pancreatic cancer The 37-year-old from Chorley, Lancashire, is calling for businesses to better educate security staff on accessible toilets after a series of experiences where she was denied access "I should be able to enjoy a night out without being question. There needs to be more information available to these companies about who needs this and why they might need it," she said At the age of 24, Victoria was fitted with a stoma after an abscess in her bowel was removed The surgery left her struggling to walk and initially unable to eat

evidence_packet.lead: You could easily miss it, but a small black plaque sits in a corner of the arrivals hall at Manchester Airport's Terminal 3 to commemorate one of humanity's greatest achievements It marks the incredible journey of Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin, who famously became the first perso
evidence_packet.summary: You could easily miss it, but a small black plaque sits in a corner of the arrivals hall at Manchester Airport's Terminal 3 to commemorate one of humanity's greatest achievements It marks the incredible journey of Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin, who famously became the first perso
evidence_packet.evidence_text: You could easily miss it, but a small black plaque sits in a corner of the arrivals hall at Manchester Airport's Terminal 3 to commemorate one of humanity's greatest achievements It marks the incredible journey of Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin, who famously became the first person in space 65 years ago On 12 April 1961, his Vostok spacecraft completed a single orbit of the Earth at the height of the so-called space race, as Russia and the US competed to make the first daring leaps beyond the heavens Just three months later, Gagarin visited Manchester to be greeted by rapturous crowds as part of a world tour on 12 July 1961. His visit is the subject of a new episode of Hidden Manchester on BBC Sounds Hundreds of people turned out to see Gagarin arrive at the airport, including Fred Garner who spoke to the BBC in 2011 "You could tell he was in uniform with like a rubber cape on. I can't believe how hard it was raining," he said

Are they benefiting from the hikes or are their own pr
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mention Christmas markets these days and the conversation often turns to rising prices – from £8 bratwursts, £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps and even £5 for a few marshmallow sticks But what do the people behind the stalls think? Are they benefiting from the hikes or are their own profits being squeezed? Traders at Manchester's Christmas markets told the BBC they were feeling the pressure of increasing bills for staff, ingredients and energy, with some saying they were making less money despite charging more One trader said it costs at least £4,000 a day to run each her four stalls, while another has cut prices to keep customers coming back Nils Borstel, 25, helps run Bratwurst King, a family business which has operated at the markets since 1999 He said a sausage that previously cost £3.50 now sold for £8, with much of the increase taking place over the past five or six years

They can only hope for milder conditions as 2026 draws to a close. Hannah Richardson reports. View 10 Images A tent in Manc Add to preferred sources News Hannah Richardson 07:15, 15 Nov 2026 The festive lights flicker on as the smells from the stalls of Market Street linger in the crisp November air. Overnight, it's dipped below zero. People are waking up on the streets of Manchester city centre at -1 In a few hours, the Christmas Markets will be packed. It's a time of year many long for - days and nights out with friends and family, office parties, fun with the kids For those sleeping rough, an already difficult life just got a lot more tough. As the month wears on and December arrives, the icy weather will continue to bite Frost covers the pavements on Friday morning (November 13). It's a beautiful start to the day, but it's bitterly cold. Commuters power-walk past sleeping bags as those curled up inside desperately try to get a few more minutes of sleep Numb-fingered and exhausted, the city's homeless face a grim winter. The pursuit ended in west Yorkshire, on the eastbound carriageway of the M62 between junction 26, near Cleckheaton, and junctio The crash involved the suspected stolen vehicle and police tactical unit cars, the force said. Part of the motorway between junctions 26 and 27 was shut for a time after the collision National Highways said the closure was in place 'due to a multi-vehicle collision'. Wearing sunglasses, heavy gold jewellery and a black hoodie, h "Look it's No Chill," he raps. "Remember days when I had no till. So I had to whip it like oatmeal. Stamps on the brick, signed up to a coke deal." Since being uploaded to YouTube in June 2022 the video has been watched 3.6m times. But more than four years on its star - real name Clint Curtis - is no longer in the music business Instead, he's behind bars at HMP Lincoln, serving a 19 year sentence for drugs and firearms offences. So was this a case of an up-and-coming musician playing a role, using bravado and exaggeration to build a fanbase? Or was it a case of art imitating life and had Curtis actually committed the crimes he was rapping about? Greater Manchester Police responded to reports of a vehicle being stolen on Wilson Street in Swinton, Salford, at aroun The car was later spotted on the M60 by the National Police Air Service, the police helicopter. It was then pursued on the M60 before moving on the M62. The pursuit ended in west Yorkshire, on the eastbound carriageway of the M62 between junction 26, near Cleckheaton, and junctio The crash involved the suspected stolen vehicle and police tactical unit cars, the force said. Part of the motorway between junctions 26 and 27 was shut for a time after the collision National Highways said the closure was in place 'due to a multi-vehicle collision'. A GMP spokesman said: "The driver failed to stop for officers, prompting a pursuit which continued onto the M62, with assistance from West Yorkshire Police "Between junctions 26 and 27 of the M62, the vehicle collided with GMP tactical aid unit vehicles, causing damage to the police vehicles."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police within north Manchester – and across GM – are utilising Criminal Behaviour Orders to punish people who cause issues with certain areas Within the north Manchester area, Sergeant Maxine Norton from the local Neighbourhood Policing Team has helped secured multiple orders this year, preventing people from entering areas they have previously committed crimes in, or otherwise caused issues This includes work with Manchester city council’s Anti-Social Behaviour Action Team (ASBAT), who assist in CBO work along with other orders such as Community Protection Notices (CPNs) and injunctions CBOs are used to target individuals who are repeat demand generators, and have been identified as often engaging in criminality in a specified area. They are given to people who have been convicted of an offence with the aim to prevent them engaging in further criminal behaviour While a CBO is a civil order, breaching one is a criminal offence, and may result in arrest, charges, and punishments including imprisonment, fines, or community service Many CBOs are done with exact specifications in mind – preventing people from entering certain areas in which they have been known to cause issues. They are typically anywhere from one to five years, but can be extended if necessary

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Brian Sinclair, 54, used his position at Nobel Foods in North Scarle, Lincolnshire, to divert stock and place false orders with manufacturers to steal from the company, police said Sinclair, of Wild Street, Shaw, in Oldham, previously admitted one count of theft, four counts of fraud by false representation and two counts of fraud by abuse of position He was sentenced to three years and eight months in prison at Lincoln Crown Court in April A proceeds of crime hearing at the same court earlier heard Sinclair made a benefit of £101,000 from his crimes, with available assets in the region of £44,000, including two pensions Recorder Anna Marie Trussler ordered the sum to be confiscated from Sinclair and to be paid to Nobel Foods in the form of compensation Sinclair, who watched the hearing via a video-link from prison, was given three months to pay back the money or face a further 12 months imprisonment

evidence_packet.summary: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026. The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area. The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications. Residents will be asked the following question: “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area. The deadline to register to vote is Tuesday 24 November 2026. Residents who wish to vote by post, proxy or who need a Voter Authority Certificate should also be aware of the following deadlines: - Wednesday 25 November, 5pm: Deadline for new postal vote applications and changes to existing postal voting arrangements. - Wednesday 2 December, 5pm: Deadline for new proxy vote applications and applications for a free Voter Authority Certificate. - Thursday 10 December, 5pm: Deadline for emergency proxy vote applications, where eligible. Residents can read the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan and supporting referendum documents online at: https://www.oldham.gov.uk/info/201235/neighbourhood_planning/2936/saddleworth_neighbourhood_plan Paper copies are also available to view at Lees, Uppermill, Delph and Greenfield libraries, Oldham Council’s reception

If more than one valid nomination is received, residents will go to the polls on Thursday 3 December 2026 to elect their new councillor. This is an opportunity for local people from all backgrounds to represent the interests of their community, raise issues that matter to residents and play a direct role in shaping the future of Royton North and the wider borough. Councillors represent the Council to the community and the community to the Council. Anyone wishing to stand for election can obtain a nomination pack from the Elections Office at the J.R.Clynes Building, Cultural Quarter, Greaves Street, Oldham, OL1 1AL, between 9am and 5pm, or they can be emailed on request by emailing election@oldham.gov.uk. Completed nomination papers must be submitted in person and cannot be accepted by email, post, fax or any other electronic method. Papers can be delivered to the J.R.Clynes Building between 10am and 4pm and no later than 4pm on Friday 6 November. Candidates are advised to book an appointment to submit their papers by contacting the Elections Team at election@oldham.gov.uk. Nomination papers must be delivered to The J.R.Clynes Building. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Primary schools have been recognised for outstanding performance in the 2026 Summer Reading Challenge Read to the Beat. The challenge, delivered by The Reading Agency in partnership with public libraries, encouraged children to discover the joy of reading through the theme Read to the Beat, celebrating music, rhythm and the power of stories. Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham. Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading. Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books. The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience. Suzanne Hudson, Senior Development Officer for Oldham Heritage, Libraries and Arts said, “It’s fantastic to see so many children across Oldham getting involved in this year’s Summer Reading Challenge. evidence_packet.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026. The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events. The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts followed by a pyrotechnic Halloween fireworks display in the area around Parliament Square from 5.30pm. Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles Kids Club. The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance. The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show. To coincide with the switch on, the Festive Fun with Peppa Cinema Experience is coming to the Odeon at Parliament Square on Saturday 14 and Sunday 15 November, at 10am and 11.30am both days. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheers to the women who changed the way we drink! Hear the hidden history of the female pioneers who drank, distilled, and defied , while enjoying cocktails inspired by them Drinking history expert Simon Sharp takes you on a journey from the invention of the pub and modern beer, to distillation and champagne – where women have been at the forefront , challenging patriarchy so we can all enjoy a drink To illustrate these stories guests will enjoy four cocktails; The Mansplainer, The Poinsettia, Bees Knees, and Hanky Panky – all invented or inspired by these trailblazing ladies, crafted with ingredients sourced from female founded and led businesses A tribute to women’s creativity and courage , this tasting celebrates the mark they’ve left on drinking culture Simon Sharp is a history geek, drinks expert, and spirits judge. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Get ready for a huge dose of boy band nostalgia as Boys Are Back Again hits venues across the UK Headlining the tour are the legendary East 17, one of the UK’s biggest ever boy bands and true trailblazers of the 90s pop era. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

The title is the Latin plural of “asylum”, which can mean both a place of refuge and an institution for the insane – and the piece plays on this plurality. Its third movement, Ecstasio , is s Between these two pieces comes a world premiere: Gabriella Smith’s How To Be A Bird , written for tonight’s soloist Pekka Kuusisto. Hailed by the LA Times as “an outright sensation”, Smith writes music drawn from field recordings and underwater microphones, looking for what she c The evening closes with Stravinsky’s Firebird Suite , one of the happiest accidents in musical history. Sergei Diaghilev, head of the Ballets Russes, saw his first three choices to score a new ballet fall through before he gambled on an unproven 27-year-old; Stravinsky himself la Four works, then, that each began as a risk on someone (to varying degrees) untested – Stravinsky in 1910, Adès in 1996, Smith tonight. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has a lot to sort out at Manchester United having been appointed the club's new manager
